detailed_description: The Gradient Generator creates CSS linear or radial gradients from editable color stops. You can choose linear or radial mode, adjust the angle for linear gradients, add or remove color stops, change stop positions, apply presets, preview the result, and copy CSS. It also provides a simple Tailwind arbitrary-value style helper for the first and last colors. The page is useful for quick backgrounds, prototypes, and design exploration. It does not validate brand accessibility or produce complex mesh gradients.
usage_steps: Choose linear or radial gradient mode.
Adjust the angle when using a linear gradient.
Edit color stops and their percentage positions.
Add or remove colors if you need more or fewer stops.
Try a preset when you want a quick starting point.
Copy the generated CSS and test it in your layout.
usage_examples: Create a two-color linear gradient for a hero background.
Use a radial gradient preview for a card highlight.
Add a third color stop to make a richer transition.
Copy CSS for a prototype before moving it into a stylesheet.

faqs.question: What gradient types are supported?
faqs.answer: The page supports linear gradients and circle radial gradients.

faqs.question: Can I add more than two colors?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can add color stops up to the limit provided by the interface.

faqs.question: Can I copy the generated CSS?
faqs.answer: Yes. The page includes a copy action for the CSS background declaration.

faqs.question: Does it generate mesh gradients?
faqs.answer: No. This page focuses on standard CSS linear and radial gradients.

faqs.question: Should I check text contrast on gradients?
faqs.answer: Yes. Test contrast in your final layout, especially when placing text over gradients.
